title: Coriantumr Remembers
summary: After recovering from his wounds, Coriantumr remembers Ether’s words. He sees how many of his people have been slain, begins to repent, remembers the prophets’ words, and mourns.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr had recovered from his wounds and began to remember Ether’s words.
Coriantumr saw that nearly two million of his people had been slain by the sword; the account also names mighty men, their wives, and their children among the slain.
Coriantumr began to sorrow in his heart.
Coriantumr began to repent, remembered the prophets’ words, saw that they had been fulfilled thus far, and mourned without comfort.

unspecified_visual_details: Coriantumr’s appearance, posture, and surroundings are not specified.

narration.text: Coriantumr had recovered of his wounds, he began to remember the words which Ether had spoken unto him.
his soul mourned and refused to be comforted.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The narration is Moroni’s account; Ether’s and the prophets’ words are remembered but not quoted here.
The deaths are reported as having already occurred, not as action occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ether or the prophets as physically present.
Do not invent dialogue, a vision, or a specific manner of repentance.
Do not stage the reported deaths as a new event.

title: Coriantumr’s Offer and Shiz’s Reply
summary: Coriantumr writes to Shiz, offering to give up the kingdom if Shiz spares the people. After receiving the epistle, Shiz writes to Coriantumr, offering to spare the people if Coriantumr gives himself up to be slain by Shiz’s sword.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr wrote an epistle to Shiz, asking him to spare the people and offering to give up the kingdom for their lives.
After receiving the epistle, Shiz wrote to Coriantumr that he would spare the people if Coriantumr gave himself up to be slain with Shiz’s own sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Separate, sequential views may show Coriantumr writing his epistle and, later, Shiz receiving it and writing his reply.
unspecified_visual_details: The locations and writing materials are not specified.

narration.text: he wrote an epistle unto Shiz
he would give up the kingdom for the sake of the lives of the people.
when Shiz had received his epistle he wrote an epistle unto Coriantumr
that if he would give himself up, that he might slay him with his own sword, that he would spare the lives of the people.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The first epistle’s writer is identified as Coriantumr by the reply addressed to him; the second epistle’s writer is explicitly Shiz.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the epistles as spoken dialogue, add wording to them, or show Coriantumr and Shiz meeting face to face.
Do not depict the proposed killing as an event that occurs.

title: Battle and Flight
summary: The people do not repent. The people of Coriantumr and the people of Shiz are stirred to anger against each other. The people of Shiz give battle to the people of Coriantumr. Coriantumr sees that he is about to fall and flees again before the people of Shiz.

explicit_facts.text: The people did not repent of their iniquity; the people of Coriantumr and the people of Shiz were stirred to anger against each other; the people of Shiz gave battle to the people of Coriantumr.
When Coriantumr saw that he was about to fall, he fled again before the people of Shiz.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The battle may be shown without gore, followed by Coriantumr fleeing.
unspecified_visual_details: The battlefield’s appearance, the number of combatants, and individual fighters’ identities are not specified.

narration.text: the people repented not of their iniquity
And when Coriantumr saw that he was about to fall he fled again before the people of Shiz.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The account does not describe individual injuries in this battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add named warriors, motives, dialogue, or graphic injuries.

title: At the Waters of Ripliancum
summary: At the waters of Ripliancum, the arriving people pitch their tents, and Shiz pitches his tents nearby. They come to battle the following day.

explicit_facts.text: The verse says “he came” to the waters of Ripliancum but does not identify him.
When they came to the waters, they pitched their tents.
Shiz pitched his tents near them.
Ripliancum is interpreted as large, or to exceed all.
They came to battle on the following day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nearby tents beside the waters can represent the encampments without establishing an order of arrival.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of “he” and the identities of the unnamed people are not established by the supplied verse.
Shiz’s appearance, the number and design of tents, and the appearance of the waters are unspecified.

narration.text: when they came to these waters they pitched their tents;
and Shiz also pitched his tents near unto them;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni (son of Mormon) is the narrator, not an established physical participant in the encampment.
The battle occurs on the following day and is not part of this encampment scene.
The audit mentions Ether 15:7, but that verse was not supplied and cannot establish the identity of “he” here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify “he” as Coriantumr on the authority of the supplied verse.
Do not add a separate visible man to represent the unresolved pronoun “he.”
Do not establish when Shiz arrived relative to the others pitching tents.
Do not depict the following-day battle during the encampment.
Do not invent dialogue or a divine appearance.

title: An Exceedingly Sore Battle
summary: They fight an exceedingly sore battle. Coriantumr is wounded again and faints from loss of blood.

explicit_facts.text: They fought an exceedingly sore battle.
Coriantumr was wounded again and fainted from loss of blood.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Coriantumr may be shown collapsing during the battle.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, combatants’ appearances, weapons, and formations are not specified.

narration.text: they fought an exceedingly sore battle
Coriantumr was wounded again, and he fainted with the loss of blood.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood, graphic wounds, or a location not given in the supplied verse.

title: The Armies Move South
summary: Coriantumr’s armies beat Shiz’s armies, who flee southward and pitch their tents at Ogath. Coriantumr’s army pitches its tents by the hill Ramah.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr’s armies press upon and beat Shiz’s armies, causing them to flee southward and pitch their tents at Ogath.
Coriantumr’s army pitches its tents by the hill Ramah.
Ramah is the same hill where Moroni’s father Mormon hid sacred records unto the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The retreat toward Ogath and the camp by Ramah can be shown as successive moments, not simultaneous action.
unspecified_visual_details: The terrain, tents, and armies’ appearances are not specified.

narration.text: the armies of Coriantumr did press upon the armies of Shiz that they beat them, that they caused them to flee before them;
and they did flee southward, and did pitch their tents in a place which was called Ogath.
the army of Coriantumr did pitch their tents by the hill Ramah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni identifies Ramah as the hill where his father Mormon hid sacred records; that earlier event is not part of the present action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Mormon or the hiding of the records as part of this scene.
Do not invent combat details, injuries, or dialogue.

title: The Survivors Gather
summary: The surviving people gather to their chosen armies. Ether beholds the gathering and sees the people of each side joining its army.

explicit_facts.text: All people in the land who had not been slain gathered, except Ether.
Ether beheld the people for Coriantumr gathered to his army and the people for Shiz gathered to his army.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The gathering may be shown as two distinct groups assembling with their respective armies.
unspecified_visual_details: Ether’s vantage point and the precise gathering place are not specified.

narration.text: Ether did behold all the doings of the people
the people who were for Shiz were gathered together to the army of Shiz.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ether beholds the events; the passage does not state that he joins either army.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular hiding place or make Ether part of the gathered armies.

title: Four Years of Gathering
summary: For four years, the sides gather people and seek to assemble all available strength.

explicit_facts.text: For four years, they gathered people from across the land and sought all the strength they could receive.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The gathering could be conveyed through people joining the opposing forces over time.
unspecified_visual_details: The specific places, individuals, and events during those four years are not described.

narration.text: for the space of four years gathering together the people

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a summary of a four-year period, not a single dated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent particular recruitment scenes, leaders, or events during the four years.

title: The Armies March to Battle
summary: When all were gathered, men, women, and children armed with weapons and protective gear march against one another. They fight all day without a victor.

explicit_facts.text: Men, women, and children were armed with weapons, shields, breastplates, and head-plates, and marched against one another.
They fought all day and neither side conquered.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The armed groups may be shown facing each other and fighting, without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The clothing styles, exact weapons, battlefield, and appearance of the people are not specified.

narration.text: they did march forth one against another to battle
they fought all that day, and conquered not.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show casualties beyond what is stated in the verse.

title: Lament in the Camps
summary: At night, the weary people retire to their camps and lament loudly for those slain.

explicit_facts.text: At night the weary people returned to their camps and lamented the loss of their slain people with great cries and howling.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people may be shown grieving in their camps at night.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of mourners and the layout of the camps are unspecified.

narration.text: they took up a howling and a lamentation for the loss of the slain of their people

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific words spoken by mourners.

title: Another Day of Battle
summary: The people fight again the next day without conquering. At night they cry and mourn for their slain.

explicit_facts.text: The people fought again the next day; neither side conquered, and at night they cried and mourned for their slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A single moment of the day’s fighting may be shown, with the night lament conveyed as a separate moment only if needed.
unspecified_visual_details: The combatants’ precise actions and the battlefield are unspecified.

narration.text: great and terrible was that day
they did rend the air with their cries

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The battle and the nighttime mourning are separate moments; avoid combining them in one image.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a victor or specific combat outcome.

title: Coriantumr’s Second Letter
summary: Coriantumr writes again, asking Shiz not to return to battle and offering him the kingdom to spare the people. The people go again to battle.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr wrote Shiz asking him not to come again to battle, but to take the kingdom and spare the people.
The people went again to battle after the Spirit of the Lord had ceased striving with them and Satan had full power over their hearts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Coriantumr may be shown writing the letter; the return to battle is a separate moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The letter’s physical form, its delivery, and the place of writing are unspecified.

narration.text: desiring that he would not come again to battle
wherefore they went again to battle.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The descriptions of the Spirit, Satan, hearts, and blindness are doctrinal narration, not a depicted visible supernatural event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Satan or the Spirit as visible figures.
Do not portray the letter as spoken dialogue.

title: Night on the Swords
summary: The people fight through successive days and sleep on their swords at night. On one night they are drunken with anger, as a man is drunken with wine, and sleep again on their swords.

explicit_facts.text: They fought all day and slept upon their swords when night came.
They fought through the next day until night.
At night they were drunken with anger, as a man is drunken with wine, and slept again upon their swords.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A nighttime camp moment may show exhausted people lying with swords; the comparison to drunkenness is figurative.
unspecified_visual_details: The camps and the people’s exact appearance are not specified.

narration.text: they slept upon their swords.
they were drunken with anger

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The phrase ‘drunken with anger’ is a figure of speech, not literal intoxication.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal wine-drinking or supernatural effects.

title: Few Remain
summary: After another day of fighting, only fifty-two of Coriantumr’s people and sixty-nine of Shiz’s remain. They sleep on their swords; the next day the survivors fight with swords and shields. By night, thirty-two of Shiz’s people and twenty-seven of Coriantumr’s remain.

explicit_facts.text: After another day of fighting, fifty-two of Coriantumr’s people and sixty-nine of Shiz’s remained.
After sleeping upon their swords, they fought with swords and shields all the following day.
By night, thirty-two of Shiz’s people and twenty-seven of Coriantumr’s remained.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The dwindling survivors may be depicted facing one another with swords and shields.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact appearance and identities of the surviving fighters are unspecified.

narration.text: they contended in their might with their swords and with their shields
there were thirty and two of the people of Shiz, and twenty and seven of the people of Coriantumr.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The count changes across the successive events; do not combine the counts into one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show or detail gore or individual deaths.

title: Preparing for Death
summary: The remaining people eat and sleep, preparing for death the next day. They are large and mighty men; they fight for three hours and faint from loss of blood.

explicit_facts.text: The survivors ate and slept and prepared for death the next day; they were large and mighty men.
They fought for three hours and fainted with loss of blood.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fight may be shown as the men tiring and falling, without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The number of people present in this particular fight is not specified.

narration.text: they ate and slept, and prepared for death on the morrow.
they fainted with the loss of blood.

prohibited_inventions: Do not show blood or graphic wounds.

title: Shiz Pursues
summary: Coriantumr’s men regain enough strength to walk and are about to flee. Shiz rises with his men and swears to slay Coriantumr or perish by the sword. He pursues them, overtakes them the next day, and fights until only Coriantumr and Shiz remain; Shiz faints.

explicit_facts.text: Coriantumr’s men regained enough strength to walk and were about to flee.
Shiz and his men rose; Shiz swore to slay Coriantumr or perish by the sword.
Shiz pursued and overtook them the next day; after they fought, only Coriantumr and Shiz remained, and Shiz fainted from loss of blood.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The pursuit and confrontation may be shown without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: The route of the pursuit and the exact number of Shiz’s men are unspecified.

narration.text: he swore in his wrath that he would slay Coriantumr or he would perish by the sword.
Shiz had fainted with the loss of blood.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The oath is reported narration, not supplied as direct quotation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent direct spoken wording for Shiz’s oath.
Do not show gore or graphic wounds.

title: Coriantumr and Shiz
summary: Coriantumr rests leaning on his sword, then strikes off Shiz’s head. Shiz raises himself on his hands, falls, struggles for breath, and dies. Coriantumr falls to the earth as if lifeless.

explicit_facts.text: After resting while leaning on his sword, Coriantumr smote off Shiz’s head.
Shiz raised upon his hands and fell, struggled for breath, and died.
Coriantumr fell to the earth and became as if he had no life.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The fatal strike and subsequent collapse may be shown with the moment framed non-graphically.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise surroundings and positions are unspecified.

narration.text: he smote off the head of Shiz.
Coriantumr fell to the earth, and became as if he had no life.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text explicitly describes the beheading; depict the action without showing severed body parts or gore.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore, blood, or Shiz’s severed head.

title: Ether Finishes His Record
summary: The Lord tells Ether to go forth. Ether goes forth, beholds that the Lord’s words have been fulfilled, finishes his record, and hides it in a manner that the people of Limhi find it. Ether’s last written words express that his fate matters not if he is saved in God’s kingdom.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord spoke to Ether and told him to go forth; Ether went forth and beheld that the Lord’s words had been fulfilled.
Ether finished his record and hid it in a manner that the people of Limhi found it.
Ether’s last written words say that whether he is translated or suffers the Lord’s will in the flesh matters not if he is saved in God’s kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Ether may be shown completing and hiding his record after going forth.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s appearance, the place Ether observes from, and the hiding place are not specified.

narration.text: he finished his record
it mattereth not, if it so be that I am saved in the kingdom of God.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord speaks, but no visible appearance is described.
Ether’s final words are written, not necessarily spoken aloud.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lord’s appearance.
Do not show the people of Limhi at the earlier hiding event.
